title: CNC drilling machine hydraulic requirements
scope_statement: Validated scope: generic hydraulic component classes, functional valve behavior, and direct port-to-port connectivity only. Pump/cylinder/reservoir sizing, pressure and flow ratings, line selection, filtration, cooling, prime mover selection, simulation and fabrication approval are explicitly deferred to the later sizing and engineering phases.
design_narrative: Repaired port-level topology for the selected fixed-pump, open-center, shared hydraulic sequence circuit without the unsupported end-of-feed position valve. A fixed-displacement pump draws from the tank and feeds both the relief valve and one shared open-center 4/3 DCV. MainDCV.A is the forward supply branch: it extends the clamp through a cap-end pilot-operated check and also feeds the drill cap branch through an externally piloted forward sequence valve whose pilot senses clamp cap pressure downstream of the clamp lock. The forward sequence valve outlet connects directly to the drill cap chamber, preserving a reversible drill cap feed/exhaust path. Drill extension speed is realized by the selected one-way flow control in the drill rod exhaust path to MainDCV.B. The shift of MainDCV from extend to retract is an external/operator or machine command outside this hydraulic topology; the hydraulic topology enforces clamp-before-drill and drill-before-unclamp ordering once commanded. In reverse, MainDCV.B retracts the drill through the free reverse path of the one-way flow control and feeds a reverse sequence valve that opens only after drill retract pressure rises, then supplies clamp rod release pressure and pilot pressure to open the clamp cap check. Open-center neutral unloads the fixed pump and vents A/B work lines for pilot-check pilot decay.

No controlled release speed, load-holding during release, or overrunning load behavior is specified; no deliberate metering requirement is therefore captured.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Open-circuit power unit with relief protection
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Tank.S supplies Pump.S; Pump.P branches directly to ReliefValve.P and MainDCV.P; ReliefValve.T and MainDCV.T return directly to Tank.R. The fixed pump is unloaded in MainDCV neutral through the selected open-center valve.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Clamp cylinder with cap-end pilot-operated check and reverse pressure sequence release
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: MainDCV extend supplies the clamp cap through ClampPilotCheck free flow for clamp extension. The cap-end pilot-operated check blocks reverse cap flow for static holding while neutral vents its pilot path. MainDCV reverse first retracts the drill; ReverseSequenceValve opens only after drill rod pressure rises, then supplies ClampCylinder.Rod and ClampPilotCheck.X to release the clamp.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Shared-command clamp-first drill-feed sequence with direct drill cap path and rod-side meter-out
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: MainDCV.A remains commanded while clamp pressure builds. ForwardSequenceValve.X senses clamp cap pressure downstream of ClampPilotCheck and opens P-to-A only after the clamp-pressure threshold. Its outlet directly supplies DrillCylinder.Cap, preserving the reverse exhaust path through the sequence valve check during retract. DrillCylinder.Rod exhaust passes through DrillFeedFlowControl A-to-B for the typed non-compensated meter-out feed; reverse command supplies free B-to-A flow for drill retraction. The topology does not claim automatic drill-end reversal; MainDCV retract is externally/operator or machine commanded.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Reverse hydraulic sequence: drill retract before clamp release
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: With MainDCV in retract, MainDCV.B supplies the drill rod chamber through the free reverse path of DrillFeedFlowControl while DrillCylinder.Cap exhausts through ForwardSequenceValve A-to-P to MainDCV.A and tank. ReverseSequenceValve remains closed until drill retract pressure rises, then opens to supply ClampCylinder.Rod and ClampPilotCheck.X for clamp release.

design_decisions.decision: Delete the unsupported EndOfFeedPositionValve and connect ForwardSequenceValve.A directly to DrillCylinder.Cap.
design_decisions.rationale: The selected two-port position valve did not shift MainDCV to retract and could block drill cap exhaust if left tripped. A direct reversible work path from ForwardSequenceValve.A to DrillCylinder.Cap preserves valid drill feed and retract exhaust. The topology therefore does not claim automatic drill-end reversal.

design_decisions.decision: Use a fixed-displacement pump with an open-center shared 4/3 DCV.
design_decisions.rationale: No energy-efficiency requirement is stated. The fixed pump/open-center combination provides a simple conventional open circuit, unloads pump flow in neutral, and vents work lines to support pilot-operated-check reseating.

design_decisions.decision: Use one shared directional command for clamp and drill sequencing.
design_decisions.rationale: A shared DCV keeps the clamp branch commanded while the forward sequence valve waits for clamp pressure; separate DCVs would make the ordering dependent on external command logic rather than the hydraulic interlock.

design_decisions.decision: Pilot the forward sequence valve from clamp cap pressure downstream of the clamp load lock.
design_decisions.rationale: The forward trigger must represent clamp actuator pressure at the workpiece rather than unrelated pump pressure. Downstream cap pressure is the selected hydraulic indication that clamp force has built.

design_decisions.decision: Place exactly one one-way flow control in the drill rod exhaust path for drill-feed meter-out.
design_decisions.rationale: The typed drilling feed decision requires adjustable non-compensated meter-out at the rod chamber during extension. The selected orientation throttles DrillCylinder.Rod to MainDCV.B during feed and allows free reverse flow for retraction.

design_decisions.decision: Use a reverse externally piloted sequence valve to delay clamp release until drill retraction pressure rises.
design_decisions.rationale: MainDCV reverse pressure retracts the drill directly while ReverseSequenceValve blocks clamp rod supply and ClampPilotCheck.X. When the drill reaches its retracted end and retract-line pressure rises, the reverse sequence valve opens to release the clamp.

design_decisions.decision: Select a single cap-end pilot-operated check for clamp holding.
design_decisions.rationale: The specified retention is static clamp force retention during drilling and drill return, not hose-burst or full power-loss protection on both chambers. A cap-end pilot check locks the clamp cap volume and is released from the sequenced clamp release line.

evidence_gaps.reason: The valid hydraulic topology enforces clamp-before-drill and drill-before-unclamp, but the brief does not provide a supported hydraulic/mechanical implementation for automatically shifting MainDCV to retract at drill end of stroke. The repaired plan therefore does not claim automatic reversal.
evidence_gaps.evidence_needed: Clarification whether retract is operator/machine commanded or requires a fully hydraulic automatic end-of-feed reversal pattern.

assumptions: Relief and sequence valve numeric settings are assigned during sizing/commissioning.
Actuator orientation is not specified as vertical or overrunning, so counterbalance load control is not selected.
Clamp extension reaches the workpiece/mechanical constraint before drill_feed_forward; subsequent forward pressure maintains force rather than requiring additional clamp travel.
The command that shifts MainDCV from extend to retract after drilling feed completion is external/operator or machine commanded and is outside this hydraulic topology.

The command that shifts MainDCV from extend to retract after drilling feed completion is outside this hydraulic topology and must be defined at machine-control/operator level if a fully automatic cycle is required.
Vertical or overrunning actuator orientation was not specified; counterbalance load control is not selected.
Detailed sizing must check actuator bore/rod areas, pump flow, pressure intensification, and whether the stated force/speed targets are achievable within the pressure limit.

research_coverage.summary: Most hydraulic building blocks are supported with real citations: open-circuit power/relief/return topology, 4-way directional control for double-acting cylinders, pilot-operated check/load-locking for the clamp, meter-out rod-side exhaust control for drill feed, clamp-pressure sequence-valve start of the drill/feed actuator, and a cited clamp-release-after-work-cylinder-retract interlock. However, the evidence is still not sufficient for the complete automatic drill-feed motion profile and whole-cycle interlock topology because it does not clearly support how completion of the forward drilling/feed stroke automatically initiates drill retraction. Since that missing phase transition is critical to the requested ordered cycle, the design should not proceed yet.

items.rationale: The findings include supported open-circuit topology: reservoir-to-pump suction, fixed-displacement pump supply, pressure relief from pressure line to tank, return flow to reservoir, and manufacturer tank/suction guidance. Citations include Bosch Rexroth, Power & Motion Tech, and Fluid Power Journal.

The findings support using a 4-way directional valve for a double-acting clamp cylinder, describe shifted P-A/B-T and P-B/A-T port logic, and identify neutral-center implications. Clamp neutral/load-holding compatibility is further supported by pilot-operated check valve evidence requiring pilot drain/venting in neutral.

The requested clamp phases have no special speed regulation beyond sizing. Clamp extension to the workpiece and pressure rise before drill/feed start are supported by sequence-valve sources; clamp holding is supported by pilot-operated check/load-lock sources; clamp release only after drill/work-cylinder retraction is supported by the Power & Motion Tech sequence-valve/interlock source.

Pilot-operated check/load-lock valves at the clamp actuator ports are supported for holding a cylinder when the DCV is centered, cross-pilot release from the opposite work line, close-to-actuator placement, and avoidance of trapped pilot pressure that can cause drift. The findings include connection guidance and safety rationale with citations.

The evidence supports the drill-feed actuator as a double-acting cylinder controlled by a 4-way directional valve, with port logic for extension/retraction and neutral-center selection principles. The meter-out evidence adds the drill-feed work-port placement needed for the feed direction.

The adjustable throttled drill-feed-forward requirement is covered: meter-out control throttles fluid leaving the actuator, and the findings support placing a one-way flow-control valve in the rod-side exhaust path for extension/feed with free reverse flow for retraction. The drill-retracted-before-clamp-release condition is also supported. The missing critical claim is how the end of the forward drilling/feed stroke automatically transitions to drill retraction, including the cited component class and connection/placement logic for that end-of-feed signal or hydraulic reversal.

Clamp-before-drill sequencing is supported by pressure sequence valve evidence, including placement in the line to the secondary actuator, external drain requirements, and bypass check valve use for reverse flow. Clamp-release-after-drill-retracted is supported by a cited Power & Motion Tech circuit using a pilot-operated check and retracted-position permissive. The remaining gap is the complete whole-cycle automatic sequence/interlock from drill feed completion to drill retraction; without that, the ordered cycle is not fully enforceable from the accumulated evidence.

The evidence supports a leak-resistant clamp holding topology using pilot-operated check valves/load-locks close to the clamp actuator, with free flow into the held chamber, reverse flow blocked until pilot release, pilot venting requirements, and a cited interlock in which the clamp remains pressurized while the work/drill cylinder retracts and releases only when pilot pressure is intentionally applied.

missing_or_weak_information: Critical missing claim: a cited automatic transition pattern for the drill-feed actuator from completed forward drilling/feed stroke to retraction, including the actuator/end-of-stroke or pressure signal component and its connection to the drill-feed directional valve or hydraulic logic.

Critical weak integration point: the whole-cycle sequence A+ clamp, B+ drill feed, B- drill retract, A- clamp release is not yet fully supported as one enforceable interlock topology; the evidence covers major subpatterns but not the feed-complete-to-retract transition.

issues.description: Evidence gap for automatic drill-feed-complete to retract command: The valid hydraulic topology enforces clamp-before-drill and drill-before-unclamp, but the brief does not provide a supported hydraulic/mechanical implementation for automatically shifting MainDCV to retract at drill end of stroke. The repaired plan therefore does not claim automatic reversal.

design_issues.description: The topology correctly implements hydraulic clamp-before-drill sequencing, clamp load locking, drill rod-side meter-out feed, and reverse pressure sequencing for drill-retract-before-clamp-release. It does not provide or claim a hydraulic/mechanical end-of-drill-feed trigger to shift MainDCV from extend to retract; that command is assumed external/operator or machine-level. This is acceptable unless the upstream requirement is clarified to require a fully automatic hydraulic drill-feed-complete-to-retract transition without electrical sensing.

design_review.summary: No functional topology errors were found against the stated hydraulic sequencing, holding, relief, metering, and reverse-order interlock requirements. The only remaining concern is a nonblocking research/requirements clarification about whether drill end-of-feed reversal must be automatic within the hydraulic topology.

validation.summary: Deterministic validation: valid. Engineering review: valid. No functional topology errors were found against the stated hydraulic sequencing, holding, relief, metering, and reverse-order interlock requirements. The only remaining concern is a nonblocking research/requirements clarification about whether drill end-of-feed reversal must be automatic within the hydraulic topology.

policy.approach: Use most of the 8 bar system allowance for clamping to reduce cylinder size, pump delivery, valve size and motor rating; this is a lower installed-power comparison case, not the preferred match to the stated 3.3 bar transition.

actuator_decisions.justification: Sizing the clamp near the upper useful pressure range reduces the clamp bore and therefore the pump flow required for the clamp speed, but requires a higher forward sequence pressure than the stated approximate transition.
The drill feed stroke is the drill cylinder force-governing phase, and the conventional rod selection is adequate because there is only one controlled drilling feed speed.

supply_decision.justification: The smaller clamp area reduces the clamp-speed flow requirement; the evaluated policy selected a 100 mm bore, 56 mm rod clamp cylinder; an 80 mm bore, 45 mm rod drill cylinder; an 11.0 cm3/rev pump delivering 14.85 L/min; a 0.25 kW motor at the checked pressure point; and NG4 valve capacity.

setting_decisions.basis: Raised so the smaller clamp cylinder develops required clamp force before drill feed is enabled; this is intentionally a departure from the approximately 3.3 bar transition statement.
